newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions call off 25-day Toulouse bus strike.
newsitem.headline: French unions call off 25-day Toulouse bus strike.

text.p: Bus drivers voted to end a 25-day strike in the southwestern French city of Toulouse on Thursday after employers agreed to cut working hours, but unions kept up public transport stoppages in four other cities.

In Toulouse, the city hardest hit by strikes that spread 15 days ago to other provincial cities, drivers agreed to resume work from Friday in return for a cut in the working week to a basic 35 hours from 38.

Bus traffic had already picked up to about 60 percent of normal by Thursday after a court last week banned pickets from blocking non-strikers from the city's two bus depots. Strikers voted overwhelmingly to return to work.

The southern cities of Nice, Cannes, Clermont-Ferrand and Sete were still hit by the strikes, which have faded elsewhere after disrupting buses, trams and Metro underground railways in about 20 provincial cities.
The unions have won concessions on working hours but employers have not given in to union calls to cut the retirement age to 55 years from 60.

"This vote to resume work is absolutely not a failure for us," said a leader of the independent Force Ouvriere union in Toulouse, adding it was an "honourable compromise". He said the deal would create 160 new jobs.
In the western city of Le Mans, drivers went back to work on Thursday after reaching a deal with employers to cut their working week to 36.5 hours from 37.
The strikes are the latest labour challenge to the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe, which last year bowed to truckers' demands for retirement at 55 after they blocked roads.
The government has said that the state pension system would be bankrupted if all workers retired at 55.
